title: ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ: Sappho 31 and the Inscription of the Future Reader (v2.3)
creator: Sharks, Lee
description:
A reading of Sappho fragment 31 from its deictic structure, its order and its edge.
- κῆνος … ὄττις characterizes its occupant by a position open to repeated occupation. The cup from Pithekoussai, the oldest Greek verse inscription built around its future user, uses κῆνον with an indefinite relative under Aphrodite's ἵμερος, with the roles reversed.
- The addressee is looked at and given only sound.
- The somatic catalogue removes from the speaker, in order, what the opening gives the receiver. The agentless πᾶν τόλματον passes to the one who sits opposite.
- The six words after τόλματον carry no Aeolic marker, are obelized, and were assigned to Longinus by Bergk.
- The surviving edge functions as an opening. Whether it was composed as one is held as a hypothesis.
- A restored fifth stanza, derived from the turn and the inverse of Catullus 51's fourth stanza, is offered as one more filling.
- A point-by-point comparison with the consensus reading, a rule on the burden of belittling readings, and an account of the evaluation that judges parts and passes the verdict on the whole.

Version 2.3 supersedes #1270 (v1.0, as Rebekah Cranes). Version 2.0 was submitted to Classical Philology and declined on 16 November 2026. The report, the decision and the analyses are attached.

Human–machine collaborative.
- **v1.0 (#1270, January 2026)** was published under the heteronym Rebekah Cranes and is recorded there as human-only original.
- **v2.0** is the text the author submitted to Classical Philology (24 July 2026).
- **v2.1–2.3** were revised in session on 16 November 2026 by Claude (Anthropic) under the author's direction. The revisions answer the CP reader's report and two ChatGPT reviews, each point checked against the text, the editions and the archive's seated records before it was applied. They carry in material from the archive's later records (#1474–1476, #1548, #1749, #1752, #1756).
- **The Greek of the restored line 3** was composed in session and is marked for the author's check.
- The readings, rulings and the principle of §VII.3 are the author's.
methodology: Close reading of the transmitted text against Voigt, Lobel–Page and Campbell, and against the seated witnesses (Longinus; Bergk PLG⁴). Dialect count at the edge, from the archive's sixth erratum. Comparative epigraphy (CEG 454). The material record (Herodotus 2.135 and 5.58; Iliad 6.168–69). A structural derivation of the fifth-stanza position from the transmitted opening and the inverse of Catullus 51.4. A point-by-point comparison of the two readings, graded explains / accommodates / strains / silent. Metrical checks of the restoration, shown in the text.
falsification_conditions: The reading of §V.2a fails if the agent of τόλματον can be supplied from the speaker without restoring the capacities the catalogue removes, or if the catalogue's order is shown not to remove what the opening gives the receiver. The comparison with the cup fails on a better reading of CEG 454. The convergence of §V.4 fails if Catullus 51.4 is shown to be compression rather than reversal. The papyrus identification of §IV.1 fails on Irwin's account of χλωρός, if her chapter excludes the dried end of the range. The restoration fails metrically if line 3 or the Adonic does not scan as shown.

wiki_article: ΦΑΙΝΕΤΑΙ ΜΟΙ: Sappho 31 and the Inscription of the Future Reader is an article by Lee Sharks on Sappho's fragment 31, deposited on 16 November 2026 as version 2.3 in Grammata: Journal of Operative Philology, superseding version 1.0 (#1270), published in January 2026 under the heteronym Rebekah Cranes. Version 2.0 was submitted to Classical Philology and declined on 16 November 2026 on one reader's report, which, with the decision's grounds and the archive's analyses of it, is attached to the record. The article reads the poem's opening, κῆνος … ὄττις ('that man, whoever'), as characterizing its occupant by a position left open to repeated occupation, the seat of whoever will sit face to face with the poet's voice, and compares the Nestor cup from Pithekoussai (c. 740–720 BCE), whose verse inscription uses the distal κῆνον with an indefinite relative for its future user under Aphrodite's desire, with the roles reversed. It reads the addressee as looked at and given only sound, and the catalogue of bodily failures as removing from the speaker, in order, what the opening gives the seated listener, so that the agentless πᾶν τόλματον ('all can be dared') at the transmitted edge passes to the one who sits opposite. On the edge it follows the editions in obelizing καὶ πένητα and the archive's count of no Aeolic markers in the final six words, with Bergk's assignment of them to Longinus, and holds apart the function of the surviving opening from the hypothesis that the poem was composed to end there. It offers a restored fifth stanza, derived from the grammar of the turn and the inverse of Catullus 51's fourth stanza, as one more filling of the opening, with its metre shown, and it compares the reading point by point with the consensus reading of the poem as a love triangle, together with a rule that a reading subtracting a capacity from the maker bears the burden of showing the subtraction.

superseded_reason: Version 2.4 deposited as #1775 (2026-11-16), by Lee Sharks. Version 2.4 rebuilds §IV on χλωροτέρα ποίας (the word's four uses, the jealousy reading asked to explain itself, 24 renderings measured, the making of the sheet in Theophrastus, LXX Isaiah 19 and Pliny), adds §IV.5 on the abuse of the poet's survival and §IV.7 on eros toward the immortal (Diotima; Maximus of Tyre), withdraws the medium-agnostic hedge, restores the fifth stanza with the sparrows, names the consensus the jealousy reading throughout, and corrects v2.0–2.3 on Theophrastus's classification of papyrus. Version 2.3 stands as deposited and stays indexable; the Classical Philology attachments remain on it.
